question: Approximately what fraction of an infused isotonic crystalloid (e.g., 0.9% saline or Hartmann's solution) remains in the intravascular compartment after 30 minutes?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This would be true for colloids, not crystalloids. Crystalloids distribute freely across the extracellular space.

Correct. Because isotonic crystalloids distribute across the entire extracellular fluid compartment (approximately 14 litres in a 70 kg adult), only about 25% of an infused volume remains intravascular after equilibration.
Half would overestimate intravascular retention of crystalloids. Only about 25% remains intravascular.

answers.text: All of it (100%) because isotonic solutions do not enter cells

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While isotonic crystalloids do not enter cells (no osmotic gradient), they freely distribute between the intravascular and interstitial compartments, leaving only ~25% intravascular.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember Starling forces and fluid compartment distribution: crystalloids equilibrate across the whole extracellular space, leaving roughly 25% intravascular. Colloids (containing large molecules) retain ~75–80%.
Correct. The '1 in 4' rule: only ~25% of crystalloid stays intravascular — this explains why large crystalloid volumes are needed to replace blood loss and why they can cause oedema.
